text_blocks.snippet: After a storm damages your roof, put safety first, [Highlight start] stop active leaks, document the damage, and contact a licensed roofer and your insurer [Highlight end] .
snippet_highlighted_words: [Highlight start] stop active leaks, document the damage, and contact a licensed roofer and your insurer [Highlight end]

list.snippet: Stay off the roof: Wet or damaged roofing is slippery and structurally unsafe; leave roof climbs to professionals.
Avoid hazards: Stay clear of downed power lines and report them immediately. If water is near outlets or light fixtures, shut off power to those rooms.

Stop indoor leaks: Catch drips with buckets, move valuables, and dry damp areas with fans to help prevent mold. If water is pooling in a sagging ceiling, carefully puncture a small hole at the lowest point to drain it into a bucket.

Check your yard and exterior: Look for missing or curled shingles, fallen branches, bent flashing, or dented gutters, downspouts, and metal trim. Check gutters or downspouts for heavy shingle granules.
Check the attic: Look for wet insulation, damp wood, water stains, or daylight coming through the roof deck.
Take photos and notes: Record the storm date and take clear photos or video of all exterior and interior damage before cleanup or repairs. Keep receipts for emergency supplies or temporary fixes.
Cover exposed areas: If water is entering or shingles are missing, have a professional tarp the damaged section (or secure a tarp using sandbags rather than extra roof nails).
Avoid rushing into a full contract: Focus on stopping active leaks first rather than signing a major replacement contract in a panic.

Hire a licensed, insured roofer: A professional inspection can spot subtle wind or hail damage, provide an estimate, and help you decide whether to file a claim. Use resources like GAF or Owens Corning to find certified contractors and review storm checklists.
Notify your insurer: Contact your homeowners insurance company promptly to review coverage, check policy deadlines, and schedule an adjuster assessment.

text_blocks.snippet: If you share the type of storm (such as wind, hail, or heavy snow) and whether you have active leaks, I can help you prioritize next steps or prepare questions for a roofer and adjuster.
